ophthalmoparesis, and myoclonus) that responded to immunosuppres-

ease that did not respond to immunotherapy and eventually became
the most prominent feature of the disease.

followed by intravenous immunoglobulins and plasmapheresis, but
with no improvement. However, he responded to a cycle of ���ve
immunoadsorption treatment (performed two to four days apart).

with recurrence of rigidity and worsening of ophthalmoparesis,
myoclonic jerks and respiratory function, but improved again with
immunoadsorption. Subsequently, he has been treated with methyl-
prednisolone (8 mg/day) and azathioprine (150 mg/day) with no fur-
ther relapses.
